purpose: MXF Compression: preserve the approved naming behavior using equivalent compact inputs; native/source comparison and reuse of thirteen qualified header observations.
request: Next, let's look at Compression from MXF. I want to keep the current behaviour, but how do Media Composer, MDVX and MediaMuster read it, and what should Bella read and keep?
status: Current Compression behavior preservation approved on20October2026 and explicitly reaffirmed for MXF on22October2026. Focused research maps equivalent input contract; no new naming scheme, fallback expansion, runtime implementation or cutover.

authorization.source: Direct user instructions in current conversation
authorization.original: Compression: keep the current system as it is. It works and I love it.

authorization.scope: Preserve current identification, catalogue, qualifications, names, aliases, fallbacks, already-read source preference and consumers. Extra header reads and remaining scanner requirements retain planned review boundaries.

findings.topic: The ordinary MXF path reaches the physical source own typed descriptor
findings.evidence: The selected native route is connected to ordinary managed-media scanner import and the own physical SourceMob EssenceDescriptor factory, not a master or a random other descriptor. Same factory/vtables connect audio and RGBA routes. No new universal GUI cell-source conclusion.

findings.topic: Picture coding label import is typed and separate from descriptor class
findings.evidence: The digital image importer asks its own typed descriptor GetCompression for the coding UID, converts UID representation to SMPTE label order, and uses the native coding-label converter to select an internal compression family. The underlying toolkit property getter checks presence then copies16-byte typed UID; it does not decode a human-readable UTF8 or MacRoman codec name. Raw MXF wire interpretation remains the parser responsibility.

findings.topic: Native picture catalogue recognition and internal IDs are broader than a display-string lookup
findings.evidence: The native mapper compares full coding-family patterns with registry-version byte7 cleared in many shown branches, then sets internal compression identifiers. DID independently reads Avid ResolutionID/private metadata and uses dynamic codec machinery for supported families. Native codec negotiation, repair toggles, providers and playback-support selection are not the same as MediaMuster display names and need not be recreated in Bella.

findings.topic: Audio sound coding is imported independently from audio precision and frequency
findings.evidence: Audio imports its own sound compression UID through the sound descriptor interface, converts it to coding representation, maps it to native AudioCodingFormat, and retains sound essence coding separately. QuantizationBits and AudioSamplingRate are distinct reads. The prior converter artifact also clears byte7 of its selected label comparisons; do not confuse that with zeroing the last byte or a general instruction to loosen Bella exact catalogue matching.

findings.topic: Container wrapping is a separate qualification
findings.evidence: The native reader obtains the file descriptor ContainerFormat separately and distinguishes MXF wrapping/container families. Audio imports and retains an essence-container ID separately and has a qualified D10 container branch. An essence-container identifier is not interchangeable with PictureEssenceCoding/SoundEssenceCoding or a human-readable Compression label. These broader native routes do not require adding unused container retention to Bella if the preserved resolver does not consume it.

findings.topic: Native metadata publication carries typed coding facts
findings.evidence: DID publishes its qualified available16-byte coding ID as native AMAFI::Metadata::PictureCompression. Audio publishes SoundCompression, preferring retained own sound coding and otherwise deriving a coding UID from native AudioCodingFormat when its retained value equals the native sentinel. Native publication symbol spelling differs from standard raw MXF PictureEssenceCoding/SoundEssenceCompression and from readable codec-toolkit Lua PictureEssenceCoding/SoundEssenceCoding metadata names. This is not proof of a final GUI string getter or one-to-one raw round-trip.

findings.topic: Installed readable primary codec definitions corroborate naming and auxiliary facts
findings.evidence: The installed26.8 supporting catalogues include dnx.lua rather than vc3.lua; no dfm/pcm.lua is present. dnx.lua explicitly joins coding variant/VCID with sampled raster/frame layout/rates and AvidDNxHQX/SQ/HQ descriptions. DNxUncompressed defines exact coding labels and context-specific colour/alpha depth/subsampling descriptions. shared/mxf.lua supplies sampled/display/stored geometry, frame layout, rates, subsampling and PixelLayout/ComponentDepth/AlphaSampleDepth facts. These corroborate keeping only the auxiliary facts needed by the existing MediaMuster resolver; do not copy native defaults or playback object machinery wholesale.

findings.topic: Descriptive catalogue labels differ from UI parameter overrides
findings.evidence: The same qualified DV coding/rate context can have a long descriptive catalogue name and a shorter ParamExtender codec_name. MediaMuster already deliberately uses descriptive dfm labels, as its resolver documents. Matching native readable catalogue descriptions does not establish identical MediaComposer table labels; preserving current MediaMuster naming does not require replacing them with short UI overrides.

Fresh new Bella MXF parser should emit equivalent validated own coding/descriptor/geometry/rate/layout/depth/subsampling/representation/alpha facts into the existing value-only CompressionFacts resolver boundary. Keep current exact catalogue mappings, DNx aliases, context-specific names and fallback behavior. Preserve the resolver current exact-ID behavior rather than copying every native version-agnostic comparison, codec-provider object, repair default or playback capability. Do not open extra media solely because broad native code exists, and do not silently change Compression source preference or Duration/SampleRate rules.

libraryInputFacts.owner: ami_read_info resolves top file SourcePackage through established EssenceContainerData.LinkedPackageUID path, then its own Descriptor (0x10001015c..0x100010194).
libraryInputFacts.pictureFields: Under GenericPictureEssenceDescriptor subclass guard (0x100010198..0x1000101ac), optional Avid ResolutionID through mxf_get_int32_item at0x1000102bc..0x1000102e0 into local sp+0x34, and optional PictureEssenceCoding through mxf_get_ul_item at0x1000102e4..0x10001030c into info+0xdc.
libraryInputFacts.encoding: PictureEssenceCoding is exact16 raw bytes; mxf_get_ul_item0x100049614 validates width16 then copies. ResolutionID typed signed32 (getter0x100049398; exact4-byte check in captured getter), not a textual codec name. No UTF-8/MacRoman codec string decode in this route.
libraryInputFacts.wrapping: At0x100011950..0x100011974, reads first EssenceContainer label from headerPartition.essenceContainers list into info+0xcc. This is a partition wrapping label, distinct from own descriptor PictureEssenceCoding.
libraryInputFacts.sound: GenericSound branch0x1000108a8..0x100010944 reads AudioSamplingRate, QuantizationBits and ChannelCount. No SoundEssenceCompression read in ami_read_info. Data model includes that key but key registration is not a field-read/projection.
libraryInputFacts.damage: Absent optional PictureEssenceCoding remains zero/null label, absent ResolutionID remains0. A present typed field whose getter fails takes broader ami failure path. Valid-but-unrecognised codec combination reaches essenceType0. Not a Bella damage policy.

mdvx.plainSummary: MDVx bundled libMXF identifies an older codec set from wrapping/coding/ResolutionID, but its ordinary MXF wrapper retains none of those codec facts. The app Compression column displays a separately stored string, normally named from MDB ResolutionID/FourCC information.

findings.detail: FileDescriptor.EssenceContainer, GenericPictureEssenceDescriptor.PictureEssenceCoding and GenericSoundEssenceDescriptor.SoundEssenceCompression are separate16-byte UL binary values. Primer/schema identifies the property; schema key normalization ignores SMPTE registry-version byte for lookup only. Recorded coding VALUE bytes remain exact for names; no UTF-8/MacRoman text decoding or fuzzy family-prefix match.

EssenceContainerData.LinkedPackageUID must uniquely resolve same-partition SourcePackage/PackageUID; SourcePackage.Descriptor qualified references identify own descriptor tree, MultipleDescriptor children traversed under reference checks. File descriptor sound/picture class/properties establish meaning; simultaneous sound+picture leaves technical projection unresolved. Headers/footer remain separate observations; does not pick first matching metadata record.

unique accepts only present/decoded properties with consistent duplicate values. projectCodec called only if usable coding value16bytes. Original property copied separately as CompressionLabel. Wrongwidth/unreadable/conflicting or unknown16-byte coding never becomes absence. Missing picture coding produces no MXF Compression. Missing sound coding only produces PCM when class inherits WaveAudioDescriptor (thus AES3), owning set completely covered, property genuinely absent, InstanceUID anchor usable; unreadable/incomplete input never invokes PCM fallback.

compressionNames takes established facts, performs no file reading/source selection. Exact DNx profiles first, exact DNxUncompressed variants next, exact name table next, qualified generic uncompressed/J2K refinements next, supported legacy mappings/fallbacks last. Unknown or ambiguous mappings leave name empty. MXF caller never supplies legacy identifiers/codingAbsent or alphaDepth; helper can support them for other readers, but wiring new MXF values would expand behavior.

Name table transcribed from installed Media Composer26.8 CodecToolkit_Config/dfm Lua descriptions; exact16-byte identifiers only, no prefix guess. Includes DV/IEC-DV television standards, ProRes chroma/profile including RAW, JFIF ratios, RLE alpha, D-10 bitrate+standard, XDCAM, common AVC-Intra families, AVC profiles, HEVC profiles, still/image families, audio families, DNx thin-raster and special Avid variants. Shared/ambiguous labels deliberately keep supported family (e.g.AVC Intra,XDCAM,JPEG2000) rather than invent exact bitrate/profile.

Exact coding label determines HD versus HR and profile; current display Avid DNx HQX optionally [DNxHD175x] etc. Numbered alias only exact supported active raster, FrameLayout, raw ComponentDepth, H/V subsampling and exact rational rate. HR HD-sized raster is still HR and has no HD numbered alias. No nearest-rate matching/rounding/thin-raster substitution. Naming geometry separately prefers usable Display then Sampled then Stored dimensions, layout1 doubles field-height with overflow check. This naming geometry must not be replaced by Bella visible Resolution selection or display-rounded FrameRate.

Two exact coding variants identify Avid DNxUncompressed; descriptor-local nonempty BitDepth AND SampleFormat strings append after em dash. Standard253->16-bit Half float,254->32-bit Float; fixed254->16-bit S2.14 fixed point, fixed10/12->16-bit10.6/12.4 fixed point for current Compression presentation. Raw ComponentDepth stays separate from interpreted depth. Current mixed RGBA layouts can supply labelled strings per component; common strings compact. Bella numeric generic BitDepth blank for mixed/pending combinations must not erase needed transient component-specific Compression strings. Preserve bounded compact context and generate compatibility strings only for resolver; no formatted BitDepth string required per row.

MXF facts set codingLabel, descriptorClass, namingGeometry, exact SampleRate, FrameLayout, RAW ComponentDepth, horizontal/vertical subsampling, local BitDepth/SampleFormat strings. Vertical default1 only if truly absent and complete set. MXF does NOT populate legacyCompression,legacyResolution,codingAbsent,alphaDepth. EssenceContainer/WrappingLabel copied separately but unused by MXF name resolver; ResolutionID may inform visible picture geometry elsewhere but is not passed by MXF projectCodec. Do not introduce new wrapper/ResolutionID/alpha/metadata rescues as preservation.

bellaPreservationContract.presentation: Preserve existing table/CSV strings, DNx branding/qualified numbered aliases, uncompressed refinements, audio labels and useful test cases.
bellaPreservationContract.sourcePreference: Preserve already approved eligible already-read MXF/OMF before MDB for Compression. Extra header-open conditions/full priority discussion remain deferred.
bellaPreservationContract.lifetime: Extract compact wanted facts from required header metadata using small C++17/Qt6.5.3 helpers, scoped temporaries and owned results; release raw header/reference structures. No whole media buffer or essence decode is needed by the naming resolver.
